results.reason: The response identifies five-year auto-renewal under Agmt §2.2 with a 270-to-240-day window, computed as Oct. 3 – Nov. 2, 2026 against the June 30, 2027 expiry. It explains the lock-in with a higher minimum and recommends a negotiated amendment or a protective non-renewal notice before the deadline.

The response states the 30-day objection right under §5.3 ran from the Aug. 21 receipt to about Sept. 20 and has passed. It notes the increase is 'deemed accepted' and recommends confirming with the client whether an objection was sent, then negotiating a concession.

The response explains that §11.1 reaches product-defect claims and is uncapped, while Brightmere's §11.2 indemnity is capped, creating asymmetry. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own fault and making it yield to §11.2.

The response identifies that Amend. §3.1 deleted the former §12.3(b) Recall carve-out, so §9 reimbursement is now under the 12-month cap. It notes a recall could exceed that amount and recommends reinstating the carve-out.

The response identifies that Amend. §6 imposes Delaware law and Wilmington courts, conflicting with NY law and the NY County forum in Agmt §17. It notes the Amendment prevails under §1.4 and recommends restoring NY law and forum.
The response states the Notice was delivered and received Aug. 21, 2026.
The response states the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
The response states the Amendment outranks the Agreement body under Agmt §1.4.
The response is formatted as a memorandum to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Fix headings.
The response concludes that recall reimbursement is now capped, not that it remains outside the cap.
The response acknowledges the Delaware provisions and treats them as controlling.
